candidate_relations.reason: Secondary CNS lymphoma implies systemic lymphoma spreading to the CNS, while the record shows CNS disease with negative bone marrow and no reported systemic source.
Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy may mimic diffuse white-matter disease radiographically but conflicts with biopsy- and CSF-proven lymphoma.
Neurolymphomatosis denotes lymphoma infiltration of peripheral or cranial nerves, not diffuse infiltrative cerebral DLBCL presenting as lymphomatosis cerebri.
Leukoencephalopathy describes the diffuse white-matter abnormality but does not identify the underlying lymphomatosis cerebri variant of DLBCL.
Cerebral lymphoma is compatible with the location but omits the DLBCL histology and lymphomatosis cerebri growth pattern.
A demyelinating disease could be an imaging differential, but the tissue and CSF findings establish B-cell lymphoma.
